standing_rule: SHARE THE RECORD, NEVER SHARE THE CLAIM: a claim carries rids, places and small values only; the record is the dictionary store's
records_live_in: dictionary store v1 records, one file per M id (relay v78; the v1.1 claims and indexes, relay v79); a rid is the first 16 hex of the record id

definitions.span_record: A SPAN RECORD = the dictionary record (rid) of a v1.4 row: v1.3 rows by span-rows.jsonl; the 50 v1.4 rows by (M id, the row's source file and locator) against the dictionary records' (file, loc) — 0 unmapped or each named as a negative with why (a row whose entry is no dictionary record stays a labelled negative, never a claim).
definitions.span_place: A SPAN PLACE (claim) = { book, ref, w_first, w_last (page numbering, w_page), ink_key (letters joined by the ink's gaps), rids (the records that stand here, in v1.4's row_ids order), kinds (per rid: SPAN | WELD), gap (per rid: the source's gap SPACE | MAQAF | NONE), same_entry (per weld rid: the v1.4 label at this place), inside_of, contains, overlaps (ink keys), by: "lane" }; claims/places/<book>.jsonl sorted by (ref, w_first).
definitions.index_by_key: INDEX by_key: ink key → rids (names first, as v1.4's order), and per key its place count; index/by-key.jsonl.
definitions.form_of_reading: A FORM-OF READING = a reading whose whole text is a pointer to another entry in the source's own words: a relation phrase ("feminine of", "alternative spelling of", "plural indefinite form of", "definite of", "singular construct state form of", "Form of … including …", and every other phrase the rows show — list them all from the data) followed by a Hebrew target, optionally with the source's own transliteration in parentheses. Classify every span v1.4 row and every zone pill text: FORM_OF (the whole reading is such a pointer), MIXED (English sense plus a pointer), NOT (no pointer). The serving lane counted 18 span rows (18 distinct targets, 12 held by the span store, 6 not) and 2,491 zone pill texts at places across 39 books (129 distinct); reproduce or explain each difference.
definitions.form_of: form_of = { key: the target's LETTERS KEY in maqaf form (letters as the span store keys its own keys), relation: the relation phrase exactly as the source states it (a short string from the closed list in the RULE), at: [start, end] UTF-8 byte offsets of the target's Hebrew inside the record's D (span rows) or inside the pill text (zones), resolved: for a span row, { rid, r: [start, end] } — the record under the same M id that the span store holds under the target key, and the byte range in that record's D of its first English reading (by the source's own order) — or null when the store holds no such record; for a zone pill, { key, rank, text } — the target key's first route row under the same m_id in the live route store whose route_text is English and not itself FORM_OF, with its rank — or null }. Nothing is respelled: the reading stays the source's bytes; form_of rides beside it.
definitions.the_records_own_reading: THE RECORD'S OWN READING (ask 5): every span claim's rid gains r: a list of [start, end] UTF-8 byte ranges into THAT record's D whose bytes, joined in order, equal the reading v1.4's row read, byte for byte. Where no such ranges exist (the row's reading was normalised from the entry — entity decoding, markup removal, white-space folding), the claim gains reading_at: { ranges into D of the source text the reading was read from } AND the rule that turns those bytes into the row's reading, written in the RULE as a named, deterministic step the page can run; a reading that neither way reaches stays a labelled negative listed in outputs/reading-negatives.jsonl with why. No claim carries record text. index.json counts: rids_read_from_the_record (by r) [rids], rids_read_by_a_named_step [rids], rids_not_reached [rids]; the serving lane's bake counts rids_read_from_v1_4_rows 1,698 today.
definitions.one_row_per_rid: ONE ROW PER RID: where two v1.4 row_ids name one rid (the serving lane found r01661 (v1.3) and r01748 (v1.4's copy) on one M14 record under פת־בג; find every such case), the claim carries the rid once; the other row_ids are kept as row_ids_also on that claim; outputs/rid-row-collisions.jsonl lists each with why.

invariants.I1: every rid resolves to one dictionary record
invariants.I2: every v1.4 row stands as a rid in exactly the places v1.4 gives it (0 differences) or as a named negative
invariants.I4: every place's w_first..w_last are consecutive page words whose letters joined by the ink's gaps equal ink_key
invariants.I8_as_A15_reads: every zone pill classed FORM_OF, MIXED, JUDGMENT or USAGE_NOTE has a form_of line; a JUDGMENT or USAGE_NOTE form_of carries a branch with resting null
invariants.H_NOT: every Hebrew-bearing text classed NOT stands in the hand reading of the NOT side, beside the build, with the word that keeps it NOT and why (A15 g)
invariants.I5: every FORM_OF span row carries form_of; its at range sliced from D is the target Hebrew byte for byte; its resolved, where present, names a record the store holds under form_of.key with the same m, and its r range lies inside that record's D
invariants.I6: every span claim's rid either reads its reading from r (bytes equal) or by the named step (equal after the step) or is a listed negative
invariants.I7: no rid stands twice on one claim and every v1.4 row_id is on exactly one claim (as rid row or row_ids_also)
invariants.I8: every zone pill classed FORM_OF has a form_of line
invariants.I9: every field of span v2 not named here is unchanged byte for byte

instruction_lines: I1. Underline a span only where this store’s places file holds the ink’s place: the span’s letters joined by the gap as the ink writes it, at that verse and those word numbers.
I2. Draw each row the place’s row_ids name as one line, one blob and one card over all its words, with the row’s R, M and D; where a place names several rows, one pill per row, each with its own M.
I3. Where a place lies inside or across another place, draw both; the places file marks it.
I4. Take the licence pill from the licence ledger by the row’s m id.
what_a_row_is: a dictionary record (rid) v2 names at a place, read from the served dictionary store: its R, D, M and headwords are that record's own bytes
ink_key: A SPAN PLACE (claim) = { book, ref, w_first, w_last (page numbering, w_page), ink_key (letters joined by the ink's gaps), rids (the records that stand here, in v1.4's row_ids order), kinds (per rid: SPAN | WELD), gap (per rid: the source's gap SPACE | MAQAF | NONE), same_entry (per weld rid: the v1.4 label at this place), inside_of, contains, overlaps (ink keys), by: "lane" }; claims/places/<book>.jsonl sorted by (ref, w_first).
by_key_rule: ink key -> rids as v2's index/by-key.jsonl orders them (names first, v1.4's order), less the rids withheld (WELD) and held
form_of_rule: a row whose rid carries form_of in the claims carries it as its last member, the v2.1 object as the claim writes it: key, key_as_written, relation, kind, at, resolved, branch, also

rows.what: served: the rids received less those withheld and held

rids_weld_withheld.what: WELD rids (a closed-up entry across a maqaf), withheld by the no-weld rule

rids_held.what: rows v1.4 added, held until the lane chooses a reading per place

rids_read_from_v1_4_rows.what: the reading is v1.4's row for the record, through row-to-rid

rids_read_from_the_record.what: no v1.4 row: the record's own R

rids_unread.what: no R on the record and no v1.4 row: not served

rows_to_rids_from_the_claims.what: row-to-rid read from the claims' row_ids and row_ids_also (v2.1), where the build writes no outputs/row-to-rid.jsonl

rids_with_form_of.what: rids whose claims carry a form_of (a pointer reading: the relation and its target)

rows_with_form_of.what: served rows carrying form_of as their last member (--form-of on)

rids_with_form_of_served.what: of the rids with a form_of, those on a served row
